name: My Player career mode, part one: menu, five saved careers, new career steps up to the district club
message: Home gets My Player between Advanced Customisation and Settings; Start new career (name, age, gender, jersey, country, state, district club) and Resume career with up to five saved careers

package com.cricketsim.logic

/**
 * One saved career of the My Player mode (Home > My Player). Part one holds only what the player chose while starting it;
 * the club's squad (players made up at random, with their own batting, bowling and fielding ratings), the matches and the
 * progress come in later parts.
 *
 * @param gender "Male" for now (the game has no women's cricket yet)
 * @param state the state, county, province or region the player chose (the word the screens use is "state")
 * @param domesticTeams the game's domestic teams of that state (one, or several: Maharashtra, Mumbai and Vidarbha)
 * @param club the district club
 */
data class CareerProfile(
    val id: String,
    val firstName: String,
    val lastName: String,
    val age: Int,
    val gender: String,
    val jersey: Int,
    val country: String,
    val state: String,
    val domesticTeams: List<String>,
    val club: String,
    val createdAt: Long
) {
    val fullName: String get() = "$firstName $lastName"

    /** One spoken line about this career. */
    fun describe(): String = "$fullName, age $age. $country, $state. $club. Jersey number $jersey."
}

/** One state (or county, province, region) with its domestic teams and the places of its district clubs. */
data class CareerState(val name: String, val domesticTeams: List<String>, val places: List<String>)

/**
 * The countries a career can be played in and their states. India lists its real states and union territories; the

 * real places of each state: they are only names, the players of a club are generated when a career starts.

    fun states(country: String): List<CareerState> = DATA[country] ?: emptyList()

    fun findState(country: String, state: String): CareerState? = states(country).find { it.name == state }

    /** Three or four district clubs of a state. India and Pakistan call them district clubs; the others, plain cricket clubs. */
    fun clubs(country: String, state: String): List<String> {
        val places = findState(country, state)?.places ?: return emptyList()
        val suffix = if (country == "India" || country == "Pakistan") "District Cricket Club" else "Cricket Club"
        return places.map { "$it $suffix" }
    }
}

ops.content:
# My Player (career mode), part one

Home > My Player sits between Advanced Customisation and Settings. It opens two choices: **Start new career** and **Resume career**.
Up to five careers are kept (`CareerStore`, `careers.json`); with five, Start new career is switched off and says to delete one;
Resume career lists them, opens one, and can delete it (confirmed).

Starting a career asks, one page each: first and last name (one page, two boxes), age (16 to 30, 16 to 19 recommended), gender
(Male selected; Female switched off because the game has no women's cricket), jersey number (0 to 999), country (India, Pakistan,
Australia, England, New Zealand, South Africa), state, district club. The word on the screens is "state" for every country:
India lists its real states and union territories (each with the game's domestic team or teams: Gujarat has Gujarat, Baroda and
Saurashtra; Maharashtra has Maharashtra, Mumbai and Vidarbha; Telangana has Hyderabad; West Bengal has Bengal); the other countries list
exactly the teams that have domestic tournaments in the game (England's 18 counties, Australia's six states, New Zealand's six
associations, South Africa's provincial teams and franchises, Pakistan's regions). Each state has three or four district clubs, named
after real places of the state (`logic/Career.kt`, `CareerWorld`); only names, the players are generated later.

Not built yet (later parts): the club's randomly generated players with batting, bowling and fielding ratings and names typical of the
state, playing matches, progress, retirement.
